quick: IV 6.75 mg bolus, then 18 mg/h x3 h, then 6 mg/h up to 45 h (max 48 h / 330 mg)
Used in pregnancy as a tocolytic to delay imminent preterm birth (its indication, 24-33 wks)
Limited data; minimal transfer expected with short IV course
No dose adjustment studied; experience limited - use with caution
No dose adjustment studied; experience limited - use with caution
Uterine contractions, fetal heart rate, maternal BP/HR, blood loss
summary: Atosiban (Tractocile) is a competitive oxytocin/vasopressin receptor antagonist used to delay imminent preterm birth in pregnant adults (24-33 completed weeks) with regular uterine contractions of >=30 seconds at >=4 per 30 minutes and cervical dilatation of 1-3 cm (0-3 for nulliparas) with a normal fetal heart rate. Given IV in three sequential stages over a total of up to 48 hours (maximum dose 330 mg). It is approved in the EU (EMA), not FDA-approved. Nausea is the most common adverse effect.
indications: To delay imminent preterm birth in pregnant adult women with regular uterine contractions of at least 30 seconds duration at a rate of >=4 per 30 minutes
Cervical dilatation of 1 to 3 cm (0-3 for nulliparas) and effacement of >=50%
Gestational age from 24 to 33 completed weeks with a normal fetal heart rate

dosage.d: 6.75 mg IV bolus injection over 1 minute
dosage.n: Uses the 7.5 mg/ml solution for injection (0.9 ml)

dosage.d: 18 mg/hour (300 micrograms/min) by continuous IV infusion for 3 hours
dosage.n: High-dose loading phase immediately after bolus

dosage.d: 6 mg/hour (100 micrograms/min) by continuous IV infusion for up to 45 hours
dosage.n: Total treatment duration should not exceed 48 hours

dosage.d: Total dose over a full course should not exceed 330 mg of atosiban
dosage.n: Re-treatment with atosiban may be considered if contractions recur

admin: For intravenous use only, administered by medical staff experienced in treating preterm labour
Begin treatment as soon as possible after preterm labour is diagnosed
Stage 1: give the 6.75 mg bolus over 1 minute using the 7.5 mg/ml solution for injection
Stage 2 and 3: dilute the 7.5 mg/ml concentrate for solution for infusion in 0.9% sodium chloride, Ringer's lactate or 5% glucose before infusing
Administer the loading infusion (18 mg/h) then step down to the maintenance infusion (6 mg/h)
Monitor uterine contractions and fetal heart rate during administration
moa: Atosiban is a synthetic peptide that acts as a competitive antagonist of human oxytocin at the oxytocin receptor (and also at vasopressin V1a receptors). By blocking oxytocin binding it lowers myometrial intracellular calcium release, reducing the frequency and force of uterine contractions and thereby delaying preterm birth.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to atosiban or any excipient
Gestational age below 24 or over 33 completed weeks
Premature rupture of the membranes after >30 weeks of gestation
Antepartum uterine haemorrhage requiring immediate delivery
Eclampsia and severe pre-eclampsia requiring delivery
Any other condition of mother or fetus in which continuation of pregnancy is hazardous
relative: Multiple pregnancy or gestation 24-27 weeks (limited efficacy/safety data; weigh benefit)
monitor: Uterine contraction frequency, duration and intensity
Amount of blood loss after delivery if it occurs (potential uterine atony)

preg: Atosiban is indicated for use in pregnancy specifically to delay imminent preterm birth between 24 and 33 completed weeks of gestation; it is not for use before 24 weeks. It should only be used when preterm labour has been diagnosed between 24 and 33 weeks of gestation.
lact: If a woman is still breastfeeding a prior infant during atosiban treatment, breastfeeding should be discontinued, as released oxytocin during breastfeeding may augment uterine contractility and counteract the effect of tocolytic therapy. Transfer of atosiban into milk is expected to be minimal. Data are limited.
renal: No specific dose adjustment has been established. Clinical experience in patients with impaired renal function is limited; use with caution.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment has been established. Clinical experience in patients with impaired hepatic function is limited; use with caution.

moderate: Drugs that increase uterine activity (e.g. exogenous oxytocin, prostaglandins) - may oppose the tocolytic effect
minor: Concomitant betamimetics - no clinically relevant interaction observed in studies
interactions.alcohol: Not applicable - acute hospital intravenous use.
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant interference with laboratory tests reported; in vitro studies showed no metabolic interaction via cytochrome P450.

emergency: Signs of fetal distress requiring immediate delivery

monitoring: Uterine contraction frequency, duration and intensity
Maternal blood pressure and heart rate
Blood loss after delivery (watch for uterine atony) if delivery occurs
Blood glucose, particularly in diabetic or gestational-diabetic patients
counsel: This medicine is given as a drip into a vein in hospital to help delay early labour
It is given in three stages over up to two days (maximum 48 hours)
You may feel nauseous, get a headache, feel dizzy or flushed during treatment
Tell the staff if you feel faint, breathless, develop a rash or notice vaginal bleeding
Contractions may return after treatment; a repeat course can be given if needed
pk: Uterine activity reduced within 10 minutes of the bolus
Steady-state plasma concentrations reached within about 1 hour of infusion
Effect maintained during infusion; course up to 48 hours
Store in a refrigerator (2-8 C); keep vial in the outer carton to protect from light
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; this record is based on the EU/EMA Tractocile Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC)
Three-stage IV regimen: 6.75 mg bolus, then 18 mg/h x3 h, then 6 mg/h up to 45 h - never exceed 48 h or 330 mg total
Unlike betamimetics, atosiban has a favourable cardiovascular tolerability profile (less tachycardia/hypotension)
Discontinue any concurrent breastfeeding of an older child, as oxytocin release can oppose tocolysis
Watch for postpartum uterine atony and bleeding if delivery occurs after treatment
missed: Not applicable - atosiban is a clinician-administered hospital intravenous infusion given as a continuous, supervised regimen, so the missed-dose concept does not apply.
overdose: Few cases reported and no specific toxicity pattern or antidote identified. There is no specific antidote; management is supportive and symptomatic. If overdose occurs, stop the infusion and treat any resulting effects (e.g. hypotension) supportively.
